question: A potentiometer is connected as shown to study the charging of a capacitor $C$ through a resistor $R$ from a DC source $V_0$. The charging key $K_2$ is closed at $t=0$ (the driver circuit key $K_1$ is already closed to maintain a steady potential gradient along the potentiometer wire $AB$). In the secondary circuit, point $A$ (the high-potential end of the potentiometer wire) is connected to the left plate of the capacitor, and the galvanometer/jockey $J$ is connected to the junction of $R$ and $C$ as shown. Hence, at balance the potentiometer measures the potential difference across the capacitor, $V_C(t)=V_A - V_{(R\text{-}C\,\text{junction})}$. The balancing length $l(t)$ from $A$ is measured at various instants. Which statement correctly describes the variation of $l$ with time?

options.B: $l$ increases exponentially and approaches a constant maximum value.
options.C: $l$ decreases exponentially from a maximum value to zero.
options.D: $l$ remains zero as a potentiometer draws no current.
